name: Garalde old-style serif
region: Venice, then Paris and the Low Countries
summary: The roman of the Renaissance book: moderate contrast, a diagonal stress from the broad-nib pen, bracketed serifs and a small x-height. It is the default text face of the long tradition and reads well for hours.

philosophy.core_thesis: A text letter keeps the rhythm of the hand that wrote it, so the eye reads a page without effort.
design_principles: Keep the stroke contrast between 2:1 and 3.5:1, measured on the lower-case o.
Tilt the stress of the o, e and c 15–30° to the left of the vertical, as a broad-nib pen does.
Give the serifs a curved bracket and a slight cup; the head serifs of b, d, h, k and l slope down to the left.
Hold the x-height at 0.58–0.70 of the cap height, so the ascenders rise clearly above the x-height.
Set the capitals at the classical proportions: a wide O, C, D and N, and a narrow E, F, L and S.
Use old-style figures (with ascenders and descenders) in running text.
anti_patterns: A vertical stress with hairlines under 0.3 of the stem
A large x-height that crowds the ascenders
Tight, negative tracking in text sizes
Lining figures in the middle of a paragraph
Fake bold or fake italic made by the software

classification.note: A Humanist (Venetian) face has a sloped bar on the e and heavier serifs; a Garalde has a level bar and more contrast. Transitional faces start when the stress turns vertical.

anatomy.contrast: Moderate: the thin parts are 0.3–0.5 of the stem, so the strokes swell and taper as with a pen.
anatomy.stress: Diagonal, 15–30° to the left of the vertical; the thinnest parts of the o are at about 11 and 5 o'clock.
anatomy.serifs: Bracketed and slightly cupped; the head serifs of the lower case are wedges that slope down to the left.
anatomy.terminals: Pear-shaped or teardrop terminals on a, c, f and r; the ear of the g is short.
anatomy.aperture: Open: the c, e and s have wide mouths, and the bowl of the a is small.
anatomy.key_letters: A small-eyed e with a level bar, a two-storey g with a large lower loop, and an M with splayed sides and serifs on top.

metrics.x_height: The x-height is 0.58–0.70 of the cap height and about 0.40–0.45 of the em; ascenders rise above the capitals.
metrics.contrast: The side of the o is 2 to 3.5 times as thick as its top.
metrics.width: The lower case is of medium width: the mean advance of a to z is 0.43–0.50 em.
metrics.figures: Old-style proportional figures in text; lining tabular figures only in tables.

setting.text_sizes: Set text at 10–12 pt in print and 17–21 px on screen; the small x-height needs 1–2 px more than a sans.
setting.display_sizes: Use the text cut up to 36 pt; above that, use a display cut with finer hairlines if the family has one.
setting.leading: Set the leading at 1.3–1.5 times the size for text, and 1.05–1.15 for titles.
setting.tracking: Set 0 em tracking in text; letter-space capitals and small caps by 0.05–0.10 em.
setting.measure: Set 60–72 characters a line for a book page, 45–60 in two columns.
setting.case_and_features: Use true small caps for acronyms, the f-ligatures (fi, fl, ff), and the italic of the family for emphasis.

pairing.rule: Pair it with a face of a different class and a similar x-height; let the serif carry the text and the sans carry labels.

pairs.role: sans for captions, labels and UI
pairs.why: The humanist sans comes from the same pen-based skeleton, so the two share proportions and rhythm.

pairs.role: a second serif for titles only
pairs.why: The vertical stress and sharper serifs give a title a little more formality without a clash of class.

reference_faces.note: Caslon is often filed as Garalde or as a late, Dutch-influenced old style. The Garamond name covers many revivals; some follow Jean Jannon, not Garamont.

evidence.title: A Specimen by William Caslon
evidence.credit: Caslon foundry broadside; scan on Wikimedia Commons

emotion.target_response: Trust and calm: the reader feels a book that was made with care and will last.

avoid_when: The text sits at 12 px or less on a low-resolution screen.
The brief asks for a cold, technical or neutral voice.

modifiers.how: Turn the stress toward the vertical, raise the contrast to 3–4:1, and sharpen the serifs; keep the proportions of the capitals.
Keep the pen-based skeleton and the open apertures; drop the serifs and bring the contrast down to 1.3:1.

sources.title: Robert Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style (Hartley & Marks, 4th ed. 2012)
